Package io.mavlink4j.transport

Class TcpClientLink

java.lang.Object
io.mavlink4j.transport.TcpClientLink
All Implemented Interfaces:
MavlinkLink, AutoCloseable
public final class TcpClientLink extends Object implements MavlinkLink
Dials out to a fixed remote host:port over TCP. The one implementation where preservesMessageBoundaries() is honestly false: a single poll(java.time.Duration) may return less than one frame, more than one, or a frame split across several polls — see MavlinkLink's own javadoc for why that must never be mistaken for "one poll = one message."

send(byte[], int, int, io.mavlink4j.transport.LinkPeer) is guarded by a write lock (unlike UDP, a plain Socket's OutputStream is not safe for concurrent writers). target is accepted for interface uniformity but not otherwise used: a TCP client link has exactly one possible destination, its connected remote, which defaultTarget() also reports.

      public boolean preservesMessageBoundaries()
      Description copied from interface: MavlinkLink

    • close

      public void close()
      Description copied from interface: MavlinkLink
      Closes this link. Idempotent. Unblocks any thread currently parked in MavlinkLink.poll(java.time.Duration) by closing the underlying socket/stream out from under it, per this module's close-to-unblock-the-reader idiom — that thread's MavlinkLink.poll(java.time.Duration) then returns null rather than throwing. Declared to never throw (narrower than AutoCloseable.close(), which every implementation here honours) so try-with-resources works without a checked exception forcing every caller to handle one.
      Specified by:
      close in interface AutoCloseable
